text:
Priya: Quick sync — we need a launch signal for the Optimize Toolkit (batching / caching / quant recommendations). Customer-driven ask from Acme: deterministic low-latency for interactive flows + clear cost savings. What should be the PRD acceptance criteria?

Teja: +1 to concrete SLOs. From ML side, propose: `latency p95 < 300ms` for single-turn seq<=128 on hosted small-gpu tier; `cost reduction >= 30%` vs current baseline; perf regression vs fp16 model: quality delta < 2% on our eval set. Also require canary eval with 10k prompts.

Sam: Runtime notes: batching helps throughput but hurts tail for small requests. We need a recommended default batching policy and an opt-out flag per route. Also need safe fallback to non-quantized variant if kernel not supported.

Maya: SRE concerns: prefix/KV cache mem growth and eviction policy. Acceptance should include max memory per shard (e.g., `<= 8GB` for a 16GB VM) and an eviction TTL. Need observability: cache hit/miss, evictions, and top-N keys trending.

Alex: Acme specifically: "we'll accept quant if 1) latency unchanged for typical calls, 2) cost down 35%+." They also want rollback hooks and an audit of outputs for 1k production prompts.

Katie: For rollout gating: suggest phases in PRD — alpha (internal + small customers), canary (5% traffic, 24h), ramp (50% 72h), GA. Gate metrics: `p99 errors`, `p95 latency`, `quality regression`, `cost delta`. Rollback triggers = any of: p99 latency +20% vs baseline, quality regression > 4%, error rate spike > 0.5%.

Priya: Draft PRD checklist (quick):
```
- MVP features: default batching heuristic, prefix KV cache with TTL, quantization profiles (2-3 safe presets)
- Acceptance: p95 latency target, cost reduction target, quality regression limit, memory/budget limits
- Observability: per-route token/cost breakdown, cache metrics, canary evals
- Rollout plan: alpha -> canary -> ramp -> GA with automatic rollback rules
- Customer deliverable: config guide and recommended presets for small/medium/large workloads
```

Teja: Additions: include a small eval harness in repo that can run A/B on customer prompts and produce a quality delta report. Also add unit test for KV cache eviction behavior.

Sam: Concrete runtime acceptance items to add to PRD: `batch size cap` default=32, `max latency inflation` budget=15% at p95, `fallback` hot path to fp16 if quant kernels fail.

Maya: Ops items: ensure cache TTL default 10m, max entries per shard 100k, metrics emitted to infra-telemetry. Also add a synthetic load test in staging that simulates spike + slow clients.

Alex: I'll loop in Acme to get their 1k prompt set for canary eval. They agreed to run early alpha.

Katie: Prioritization ask: do we ship all three (batching, caching, quant) together for MVP or break into two milestones? My vote: ship batching + caching MVP, roll quant as an opt-in experimental with a strict canary. 

Priya: Leaning same as Katie — quant has higher risk. We'll scope PRD MVP = batching + prefix cache + observability + rollout playbook. Quantization included as experimental feature with its own mini-RFC and acceptance checklist.

Teja: Agree. I'll draft the quant mini-RFC and include recommended quant profiles and eval checklist.

Sam: I'll add the runtime knobs and fallback code paths to the RFC so devs can opt-in per-route.

Maya: I'll write the staging load test script and memory guardrails for PRD.

Priya: Action items: Teja = quant RFC draft by EOW; Sam = runtime flags + default batching heuristics PR by Wed; Maya = staging test + cache limits by Thu; Katie = rollout playbook + gating thresholds doc by Fri; Alex = confirm Acme prompts by Tue. Reaction poll: :thumbsup: for MVP split (batching+caching first) or :thumbsdown: for all-in?

OpsBot: deploy-bot: reminder — RFC templates available at https://internal.redwood/rfcs. Auto-created checklist issue #OPT-231 for tracking.

Priya: Thanks all — quick async sync for PRD drafting. If no objections by EOD, I'll lock scope and create the PRD draft. :eyes:
